title: Collection sweep span
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$ with $k$ work tapes, and choose a symbol $a_0\in\Gamma$. Let $x$ be a word over the enlarged sweep alphabet, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on the word obtained by retracting each symbol of $x$ to $\Gamma$. Suppose $c$ is in state $q$, and every work-tape head is at or to the right of an integer $a$. For any integers $a,z$ and any $n\in\mathbb N$, the single-tape simulator started from the encoded configuration of $c$ reaches, after $1+nk$ steps, the forward-sweep configuration at frontier $z+1+nk$, with state recording $q$ and the read information at coordinate $a+n$. Its left stack is the reversed encoding of the read-marked blocks at coordinates $a$ through $a+n-1$, followed by a boundary marker, its right stack is the boundary marker, and throughout these steps the work-tape head stays between $z$ and $z+1+nk$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
$x$ is a word over the enlarged sweep alphabet
$c$ is a configuration on the retracted word
Every work-tape head of $c$ is at least $a$
